Alex — quick technical notes to answer your questions and to make the sandbox -> prod transition smooth: 

- Rate ceilings: sandbox comes with soft ceilings expressed in tokens/sec and concurrent request limits (we throttle rather than drop). For the pilot we’ll set sandbox to the higher profile (500 RPS / 2,000 concurrent tokens) so your perf runs are representative. Production will be enforced as hard limits tied to API keys and plan (we’ll provide quota tokens and overage behavior in the SLA).
- Burst handling: we support short-lived bursts via a token bucket algorithm with a 30s smoothing window; sustained bursts are subject to rate-limit responses (429). We can provision higher burst capacity for the pilot if you expect traffic spikes > 180 QPS for longer than a minute.
- Caching: for your short-summary endpoint we strongly recommend prefix/KV caching for identical or similar prompts — depends on how deterministic the prompt+context are. Typical savings: 15–40% token reduction for high re-use. I can add cache headers and TTL suggestions to the endpoint mapping doc.
- Example curl (sandbox):
  curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate-short
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <SANDBOX_KEY>'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"prompt":"<payload>","max_tokens":400}'

If you confirm the exact burst window and the expected concurrency pattern we’ll pre-configure the sandbox limits accordingly.

—Ben
